items.title: Shape raw material into a long-form draft

items.output: A structured draft with source notes, open questions, and editorial choices.
items.boundary: The creator owns the point of view, factual verification, voice, and final edit.

items.title: Repurpose approved work by channel
items.job: Start from the final source piece and create channel-specific variations without changing its central claim.
items.output: Editable newsletter, social, script, and visual-copy drafts tied to the source piece.

items.title: Prepare a release package
items.job: Bring copy, visual requirements, metadata, links, and a publishing checklist into one review queue.
items.output: A release-ready folder, metadata sheet, asset checklist, and promotion brief.
items.boundary: Floatboat prepares the package; the creator controls accounts, rights, timing, and publication.

faq.title: Creator AI workspace questions
faq.description: Creators need control over voice, sources, rights, channel fit, and what actually gets published.

items.question: Is Floatboat a writing app or social scheduler?
items.answer: It is an Agent Workspace for the work around creation. You can continue using your preferred editor and publishing tools while Floatboat organizes inputs, drafts, adaptations, and review steps.

items.question: Will every channel version sound the same?
items.answer: It should not. Define the audience, format, length, voice, and purpose for each channel, then review each result against the approved source rather than requesting generic repurposing.

items.question: Can it learn from my existing work?
items.answer: You can provide selected examples and a style guide, but the creator should still review whether a draft reflects the intended voice instead of treating imitation as guaranteed.

items.question: How do I prevent invented facts or citations?
items.answer: Keep research tied to inspectable sources, distinguish source notes from original commentary, and verify every factual claim before publication.

items.question: What about copyrighted or licensed source material?
items.answer: Use only material you are allowed to process and adapt. Permissions, attribution, licensing, and fair-use decisions remain with the creator.

items.question: Will Floatboat publish automatically?
items.answer: The recommended workflow ends with a release package for review. Account access, publication, and irreversible channel actions should remain explicitly approved.

items.question: What is a good first creator workflow?
items.answer: Choose one finished long-form piece and adapt it into two clearly different channels. Judge fidelity and usefulness before saving the process.

finalCta.title: Keep the idea connected to every format
finalCta.description: Bring the material behind one finished or nearly finished work. Build the next draft and release package without losing the source or your editorial control.
